question: What early-ADMET picture can I put together for a single compound right after a screening hit, given just its SMILES string (e.g. CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O for aspirin) and no in vivo PK data yet — covering physicochemical properties like molecular weight, cLogP, TPSA, and rotatable bond count, flags from standard rule sets (Lipinski, Veber, Egan, Muegge) and structural alerts like PAINS or BRENK, plus any measured CYP inhibition, hERG, microsomal stability, plasma protein binding, permeability, or solubility data reported for the same or closely related scaffolds — with each conclusion traceable back to the specific descriptor, rule, or assay record behind it?

I'm running a drug repurposing screen and want to shortlist approved compounds worth testing against KRAS G12C in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Can you pull together disease-target genetic and expression evidence, known bioactivity of approved drugs against KRAS or its pathway members, off-target/interaction liabilities, and current approved indications, then reconcile everything into one table of 10-20 clinical-stage candidates with the supporting evidence cited per row?

I'm developing a small-molecule drug for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis and just got promising Phase 1b safety and biomarker data showing IL-13 pathway suppression; can you help me turn that into a structured first-draft plan for the Phase 2 study, covering the applicable FDA regulatory pathway, a survey of competing therapies and prior trials in this indication, a justified sample-size calculation for an expected 30% improvement in EASI score over placebo, and an initial outline of the study procedures and design?

I need to know what my MEK1/2 hit does before I sink more time into it — can you pull together the disease links and known mechanism, protein domains and PTMs, subcellular localization, structural confidence regions, and CRISPR essentiality across cancer cell lines (plus drug sensitivity if available), and hand me a short cited summary instead of me hopping between four different sites?

How do I go from a disease name to a ranked list of the genes most strongly implicated in it, and then get that gene list turned into a clean summary of the biological processes and pathways (like GO/KEGG/Reactome terms) those genes are significantly enriched in, ideally as two exportable tables I can trust are backed by real statistics rather than a hallucinated summary?

I'm sitting on a folder of de-identified clinic notes for a few hundred patients and need to build a registry table — one row per patient with columns like diagnosis, stage, prior lines of therapy, biomarker status, and acute symptoms — pulled out of the free text according to a fixed codebook of allowed values and abstraction rules. How can I get this done so that each filled-in cell is traceable back to the specific note ID and quoted sentence it came from, and so the whole extraction process is written down and rerunnable rather than something a person just did once by hand?

I'm trying to benchmark a Caco-2 permeability prediction model against the published leaderboard for that endpoint, using the standard scaffold split and the official evaluation metric so the number is directly comparable — can you help me pull the frozen dataset split, run a Morgan-fingerprint plus random-forest baseline, and report the score in the same format as the leaderboard, all in one go?

I need help identifying a bacterial isolate from a 16S sequence I got back from colony PCR using the 27F/1492R primers (also have a version pulled from a draft genome assembly). I want to compare it against type-strain references and get a properly justified species- or genus-level call using the standard identity thresholds, but I want to avoid false confidence from partial-length or chimeric reads, avoid searching a database full of misannotated environmental clones, and end up with a ranked hits table (identity, coverage, assignment) plus a clear record of exactly which reference database version was used so the result is reproducible later.

I'm designing CRISPR-Cas9 knockout guides for a specific gene (say, human TP53) and want to make sure I pick good ones instead of just eyeballing candidates — I need guides landing in early constitutive coding exons, next to valid PAMs, with strong on-target activity and low off-target risk, ideally favoring ones with prior experimental validation, and I want a clear record of why each candidate was chosen so I can order oligos and cite the design in my methods.

I'm interested in a specific cancer context — say, cell lines carrying an SS18::SSX fusion, or ones with low ATP1B1 expression — and I want to find genes whose CRISPR knockout is selectively lethal there but not in other lineages, using genome-wide dependency scores across hundreds of profiled cancer cell lines paired with their mutation, copy-number, and expression data. I need to rank candidate genes by selective killing effect with proper statistical correction, filter out genes that are essential everywhere or whose apparent dependency is just a copy-number artifact from CRISPR cutting amplified DNA, and keep track of exactly which version of the underlying dataset I used so the ranking is reproducible. How should I approach this?
